issue.body:
## Description
Implement a premium dark frosted glass design system for all portfolio components. Includes adding a dynamic scroll transparency effect, integrating a Personal Identity panel, and cleaning up the Mac layout.

## Tasks
- Add Glassmorphism classes to index.css
- Restructure App.tsx layout containers
- Implement IntersectionObserver scroll logic
- Remove old Mac Dock
- Integrate PersonalIdentity component

issue.title: [test] : add coverage thresholds and cover the two untested runtime paths
issue.body:
`npm run test:coverage` on main today reports **94.06%** statements across 111 tests, and the
uncovered lines are the riskiest code in the package:

    src/index.node.ts            0%      lines 1-6
    src/internal/random.ts    66.66%     lines 9-17, 27-38

- `src/index.node.ts` is the Node-specific entry point that fixes the Node ESM crypto bug — the
  one the design doc calls a "great war story". It is never imported by a test.
- `random.ts` lines 9–17 are `loadNodeCrypto()`, and 27–38 are the `node:crypto` fallback plus
  the "no secure random source found" throw. These are exactly the paths that run on the
  runtimes we can't easily test, and they've never been executed by the suite.

Nothing stops coverage regressing either — CI runs `npm test`, not `test:coverage`.

## What to do

1. Add a test that imports `src/index.node.js` directly and asserts it generates valid IDs
   (this also proves `setBytesProvider` is wired up).
2. Add tests that stub `globalThis.crypto` away — `test/random.test.ts` already uses `vi` and
   has a "bytes provider indirection" block to model this on — to exercise the `loadNodeCrypto()`
   fallback and the throw when no source exists.
3. Set `coverage.thresholds` in `vitest.config.ts` at no lower than the numbers you achieve, and
   add a coverage run to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` so the thresholds are enforced.

## Acceptance criteria

- `src/index.node.ts` and the `random.ts` fallback/throw paths are covered.
- Thresholds committed and enforced in CI; a deliberate coverage drop fails the build.
- Existing tests unchanged in behaviour.
- No CHANGELOG entry needed (tests only).
